name: Secure Campus Wi-Fi Management System
description: Design a secure campus Wi-Fi management system for a university that provides wireless access to students, faculty, staff, and guests across academic buildings, hostels, laboratories, and administrative offices. The system should use centralized authentication, role-based access control, separate guest access from internal university resources, monitor active wireless sessions, detect repeated authentication failures and unauthorized access attempts, and generate security alerts. Network administrators should be able to configure wireless access policies, review connected devices, revoke access, and inspect audit logs. The solution should support university-managed and approved personal devices and remain secure, scalable, reliable, and manageable across multiple campus locations.
review_constraint: CyberSRS should not invent specific Wi-Fi standards, VLAN IDs, authentication protocols, session limits, or alert thresholds unless confirmed.

name: Secure University Email Security Gateway
description: Design a secure email security gateway for a university that protects students, faculty, staff, and administrators from phishing, malicious attachments, spoofed messages, and suspicious links. The system should inspect incoming and outgoing email traffic, detect suspicious messages, quarantine potentially harmful emails, generate security alerts, and allow authorized administrators to review and release quarantined messages. The platform should maintain audit logs of filtering decisions and administrator actions, integrate with the university identity system, and provide a dashboard for monitoring email security events. The solution should be secure, reliable, scalable, and manageable for university-wide deployment.
review_constraint: CyberSRS should not invent antivirus vendors, exact quarantine duration, attachment-size limits, specific ML models, or response-time SLAs unless confirmed.

name: Secure Server and Endpoint Monitoring Platform

The platform should detect unusual login behavior, repeated failed authentication, suspicious process activity, and unauthorized configuration changes. Security administrators should be able to review alerts, investigate affected devices, record investigation notes, change alert status, and isolate compromised endpoints when necessary. The system should maintain audit logs of security events and administrator actions and provide a centralized dashboard for monitoring security status across multiple campus locations.

name: Secure University Network Firewall Management System
description: Design a centralized firewall management system for a university that manages firewall policies across academic, administrative, research, hostel, and guest networks. The system should allow authorized network administrators to create, review, update, and revoke firewall rules, enforce access restrictions between network segments, monitor blocked and allowed traffic, and generate alerts for suspicious or unauthorized communication attempts. The platform should maintain audit logs of firewall policy changes and administrative actions, provide a dashboard for reviewing network security events, and support multiple campus buildings. The solution should be secure, scalable, reliable, and manageable.
